controls.statement: Trust zones (logical network "Spaces") are enforced; cross-zone traffic flows only via governed integration layers (gateway/bus).
Service addressing & discovery are unified and consistent across environments; intra-zone shortcuts are not used externally.
Service boundaries are clear; no circular dependencies; services are right-sized; each service owns its data.
Architecture avoids long synchronous chains; event-driven or queued handoffs are used where appropriate.
API/event contracts are defined and versioned; consumers are notified before breaking changes take effect.
Messaging has durability (persistence/replication/retention) with a defined DLQ strategy and triage.
Startup resilience: services handle missing dependencies; autoscaling defined with minimum replicas.
Legacy integrations are isolated behind an anti-corruption layer; migration path is defined.
Data are classified with named owners; controls are proportional to classification.
Encryption in transit (TLS/mTLS) and at rest with managed keys and rotation is designed in.
Handlers and workflows are idempotent; duplicate detection/suppression is in place where needed.
Cross-service transactions use Sagas/compensations; 2PC is avoided; prefer intra-service ACID first.
Retention/deletion policies exist per data class; minimization is applied to collection/storage.
Consistency model is documented; UX handles staleness/conflicts; event-sourcing considered where appropriate.
Retries use exponential backoff + jitter; default exception handling and safe error models exist.
Circuit breakers/bulkheads protect dependencies; non-critical features have fallback/degraded modes.
Asynchronous semantics are defined: ordering, delivery guarantees, ack/visibility timeouts; DLQs are monitored.
Shared integration layers (gateway/bus) are high-availability and contain errors to prevent cross-zone failure propagation.
All mutating endpoints enforce an Idempotency-Key; concurrency controls (locks/optimistic concurrency) are in place.
Timeouts on all calls; health probes; explicit failover/multi-AZ strategies for critical paths.
Quotas and autoscaling are defined; rate-limits enforced at edges; minimum capacity documented.
Caching/CDN/back-pressure patterns are applied where appropriate; performance guardrails are defined.
All communications use TLS/mTLS; service identity is verified (e.g., mesh-issued certs).
Central IdP (OIDC/OAuth2) is used; MFA enforced on privileged/admin paths; tokens are short-lived.
RBAC/ABAC governs APIs and publish/consume on messaging; least privilege is applied.
Authorization is centralized at gateway/mesh via policy-as-code; shared integration services are governed.
Secrets are stored in a secret manager; keys/certs rotate automatically; no secrets in code/logs.
Applicable regulatory controls (e.g., privacy/financial) are identified with evidence of design alignment.
Least privilege extends to CI/CD, VCS apps, chat-ops, and third-party tooling; periodic reviews are scheduled.
Structured centralized logs with correlation/trace IDs; administrative access is logged.
Metrics/SLOs and dashboards cover service health and event-flow anomalies; alerts are actionable.
ASVS-aligned security tests and negative tests from threat-modeling are planned in the test strategy.
SbD controls are verifiable in test (isolation, mTLS, authZ denials, rate-limit behavior).
OpenAPI/AsyncAPI and event catalogs are published; ADRs/runbooks are current.
A documented Incident Response plan (roles, comms, evidence handling) exists and is rehearsed.
Audit log retention ≥12 months with tamper-evidence and a searchable hot window is defined.

scoring.escalateWhen: any critical control is No, or total score >= 6, or any escalation trigger applies (sensitive/regulated data, new external exposure, novel technology, Tier-1 impact)
